title: Barkeep on the Borderlands - A Fantasy Pubcrawl
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zpX-Xs1a9MY

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at Barkeep on the Borderlands, W.F. Smith's Kickstarted zine from Prismatic Wasteland, and it may be the most purely delighted he sounds in this stretch of the channel. The premise is exactly what the title promises: the adventuring party is now a jolly crew, and the dungeon is a district of pubs.

The frame is a poisoned monarch and a six-day deadline. The antidote — clear as gin, smelling of a burglar burnt alive by dragon fire, turning royal blue — was misdelivered to one of the bars, and you are racing the monarch's own heir to find it. Meanwhile the Raves of Chaos run through the keep like Mardi Gras, each day carrying its own d6 tables of pangoblin pranks and rumours. Sobriety is a usage die stepping down from d12 to blackout.

It's built as a point crawl: every pub's page lists travel times and page numbers for its neighbours, plus guests, side quests, what the proprietor is doing, signature drinks and a 2d6 situation. The pubs carry it — a gingerbread dive with black smoke pouring out, a watchtower slung from hot air balloons, an undead dance club, a host club serving the lonely partners of adventurers. Written for Errant or Cairn, easily soloed, and easily looted for pubs alone.

----

Barkeep replaces the dungeon's rooms with pubs and keeps the crawl structure intact. What else would survive that swap — a market, a library, a fleet of ships?
